text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Terrorists hit army target in another bomb blast in Lagos; eight soldiers injured and authorities begin investigations.
- Private airlines resolve to increase domestic flight fares by 200 percent from next Monday compared with the 40 percent approved by government.
- Twenty buildings burnt in Amukoko, a shanty town in Lagos, after a road tanker loaded with petrol overturns and catches fire.
- Government is yet to pay fees of $3 million to agents commissioned last year to carry out pre-shipment inspection of crude oil before it is exported.
- A four-man team of the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation UNIDO arrives to carry out mid-term assessment of Nigeria's industrial development programmes.
- Three banks to stake $8 million in an international debt fund to be listed on Nigerian stock exchange next week.
- Former Nigerian ruler Ernest Shonekan, chairman of Vision 2010 committee planning Nigeria's future, says the populous nation must expand its economy in order to reduce poverty.
- Police investigating clearance of 2,500 containers from ports without import-duty reports in 1995 have arrested about 50 staff of Nigerian Port Authority.
- Manufacturers Association of Nigeria recommends to government to privatise the three paper mills in the country or lease them out to operators that can manage them better.
- French trading group CFAO restructures board of directors of its Nigerian subsidiary with a new managing director.
